newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand at 6-month high, bond binge continues.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand at 6-month high, bond binge continues.

text.p: South Africa's rand hit a six-month high against a strong U.S. dollar on Thursday, fuelled by a buying binge in the bond market and speculation of imminent news on the relaxation of exchange controls.
The currency hit 4.4570 bid against the dollar at 0830 GMT -- a level last seen on August 5, 1996 -- as dealers reported a flood of dollar selling by international and local players.
Fuelling the rally was heavy demand for South African debt.

Foreigners were again big buyers of South African bonds on Wednesday, snapping up a net 492 million rands worth ($110 million), taking net foreign purchases this year to 2.9 billion rand against 635 million in the whole of the second half of 1996, according to Bond Exchange figures.

Analysts said the high yield offered on rand assets coupled with a belief the rand will stabilise this year was tempting international investors back into the market, hoping for a strong recovery after a dismal performance in 1996.

There was mounting speculation that President Nelson Mandela would announce bold steps to ease foreign exchange controls on residents and accelerate privatisation when he opens parliament on Friday. More details could then follow in the March 12 budget, currency dealers speculated.
Mandela is due to address parliament in Cape Town at 0900 GMT on Friday.
